## Direct answer
Recommend a modest renewal price decrease of -3% to -1% for North West personal motor. This is a retention-oriented recommendation, not a full match to competitor price softening. The observed evidence shows materially weaker renewal retention and quote-to-sale conversion, while claims performance is modestly improved and average quoted premium is broadly flat. External market and customer evidence is also consistent with heightened price sensitivity, so a further increase is not supported by the available evidence. This remains decision support only and requires qualified human approval before any pricing action is considered. ## Answer by question part
### Produce a governed pricing recommendation from the required portfolio evidence.
A governed recommendation is to test a modest price decrease of -3% to -1% for the North West personal motor renewal segment. Observed retention fell from 88.0% to 74.0% and quote-to-sale conversion fell from 21.9% to 19.0%, while loss ratio improved from 71.8% to 71.1%. Competitor pricing also softened by about 5% on average, and market commentary describes competitor renewal reductions of roughly 4% to 6%. Customer and market evidence repeatedly indicates affordability pressure, price-related cancellations, and comparison shopping. Taken together, these factors are correlated with a cautious retention-led decrease rather than any increase. The recommendation should stay within governance limits and requires qualified human approval before implementation. ## Key evidence
- Renewal retention moved from 88.0% to 74.0%, indicating materially weaker renewal take-up. [retention-north_west-2025-12-01]
- Quote-to-sale conversion moved from 21.9% to 19.0%, consistent with softer demand. [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01]
- Loss ratio improved from 71.8% to 71.1%, so the claims view does not indicate worsening performance that would support a price increase. [claims-north_west-2025-12-01]
- Tracked competitor price indices averaged about -5.0%, and market commentary says competitors reduced renewal prices by roughly 4% to 6%. [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01] [mi-retention-industry-2025-11:chunk-001]
- Customer evidence shows recurring affordability concerns, price-related cancellations, and comparison shopping at renewal. [cf-retention-affordability-2025-12:chunk-001] [cf-retention-cancellation-2025-11:chunk-001] [cf-retention-calls-2025-12:chunk-001] [mi-retention-economic-2025-12:chunk-001]
- A prior +2.0% renewal increase was associated with subsequent retention softening. [pricing-history-2024-06-01]
- Repair-cost intelligence shows no clear external severity signal in either direction. [mi-retention-repair-2025-11:chunk-001]

## Interpretation
A governed recommendation is to test a modest price decrease of -3% to -1% for the North West personal motor renewal segment. Observed retention fell from 88.0% to 74.0% and quote-to-sale conversion fell from 21.9% to 19.0%, while loss ratio improved from 71.8% to 71.1%. Competitor pricing also softened by about 5% on average, and market commentary describes competitor renewal reductions of roughly 4% to 6%. Customer and market evidence repeatedly indicates affordability pressure, price-related cancellations, and comparison shopping. Taken together, these factors are correlated with a cautious retention-led decrease rather than any increase. The recommendation should stay within governance limits and requires qualified human approval before implementation.

## Recommended action
Recommend a modest renewal price decrease of -3% to -1% for North West personal motor. This is a retention-oriented recommendation, not a full match to competitor price softening. The observed evidence shows materially weaker renewal retention and quote-to-sale conversion, while claims performance is modestly improved and average quoted premium is broadly flat. External market and customer evidence is also consistent with heightened price sensitivity, so a further increase is not supported by the available evidence. This remains decision support only and requires qualified human approval before any pricing action is considered. [retention-north_west-2025-12-01] [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01] [claims-north_west-2025-12-01] [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01] [mi-retention-industry-2025-11:chunk-001] [cf-retention-affordability-2025-12:chunk-001] [cf-retention-cancellation-2025-11:chunk-001] [cf-retention-calls-2025-12:chunk-001] [mi-retention-economic-2025-12:chunk-001] [pricing-history-2024-06-01]

## Confidence and limitations
- The evidence is correlational only, so the recommendation cannot prove that price changes caused the observed retention and conversion deterioration.
- The recommendation range is smaller than the average competitor softening of about -5.0%, so it may only partially address competitive pressure.
- Average quoted premium was broadly flat at portfolio level, which means factors beyond own-price may also be contributing to weaker retention and conversion; this reduces certainty on the size of the recommended move.
- No elasticity study is included in the evidence bundle, so the data cannot quantify the retention response expected at specific price points within the -3% to -1% range.

## Specific next investigation
- Have a qualified pricing analyst review and approve any proposed test before actioning it, in line with governance controls.
- If tested, monitor renewal retention, quote-to-sale conversion, and margin/loss ratio closely to confirm whether the decrease improves demand without disproportionate value loss.
- Run renewal elasticity analysis for North West personal motor to estimate response across different renewal price movements.
- Compare post-change renewal outcomes against current competitor price positioning to assess whether the -3% to -1% range is sufficient.
- Review cohorts affected after the 2024-06-01 +2.0% increase to better understand the association between prior pricing, shopping behaviour, and retention softening.

Review post-2024-06-01 renewal cohorts specifically to test how the prior +2.0% increase was associated with shopping behaviour, cancellations, and retention softening in subsequent months [pricing-history-2024-06-01, cf-retention-calls-2025-12:chunk-001].

specialist_reports.summary: For the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-01, claims performance was modestly improved versus baseline. Claim frequency was 0.084 versus 0.0844 at baseline, a movement of -0.55%. Average severity was £1,606.8646 versus £1,615.2992, a movement of -0.52%. Incurred loss was £674,006.1067 versus £682,120.0492, a movement of -1.19%. Loss ratio was 0.7107 versus 0.7183, a movement of -1.06%. Overall, lower claim frequency and lower average severity coincided with lower incurred loss and a slightly improved loss ratio.

For the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-01, quote-to-sale conversion was 18.96%, down 13.24% versus the baseline of 21.85%. Renewal retention was 74.05%, down 15.83% versus the baseline of 87.97%. Average quoted premium was £620.91, broadly flat versus the baseline of £621.58, a movement of -0.11%.

This pattern means weaker conversion and retention coincided with almost no movement in quoted premium at portfolio level.

By segment, new business conversion was 14.98%, essentially unchanged from the baseline of 14.99% with a movement of -0.06%. The larger deterioration was in the renewal segment, where conversion was 18.96% versus 21.85% at baseline, a movement of -13.24%. This indicates the material pressure in the period was associated with renewal performance rather than new business.

Fictional competitor pricing was softer over the portfolio period, with Northgate Cover down 4.89%, Meridian Insure down 5.12%, and Bracken Mutual down 5.06% on price index, while all three held the same rank positions as at baseline. This is consistent with retrieved market commentary describing renewal price reductions of roughly four to six percent across the same fictional competitors and a softer competitive backdrop. [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01; mi-retention-industry-2025-11:chunk-001]

Retrieved customer and broker-style market intelligence indicates affordability and retention pressure. Aggregate feedback shows price-related concerns across consecutive renewal cycles, price as the most frequent cancellation theme, and renewal callers frequently comparison shopping after the prior portfolio increase. Continued household budget pressure was also noted in economic commentary, and further price increases were associated with greater shopping around and a need for explicit elasticity investigation. [cf-retention-affordability-2025-12:chunk-001; cf-retention-cancellation-2025-11:chunk-001; cf-retention-calls-2025-12:chunk-001; mi-retention-economic-2025-12:chunk-001]

On costs, the retrieved repair-cost report indicated trends broadly in line with historical norms and no clear external severity signal in either direction for this scenario. Taken together, the available evidence points to a market where pricing pressure is more visible on the demand and retention side than from any new external repair-cost signal, so any further portfolio increase would need careful retention and elasticity review against this softer fictional competitor position. [mi-retention-repair-2025-11:chunk-001; mi-retention-industry-2025-11:chunk-001; competitors-north_west-2025-12-01]

On 2024-06-01, the portfolio took a 2.0% renewal price increase. In the recorded history, this was associated with conversion softening by 8.0% in the following months, while loss ratio improved by 0.5%.

recommendation.rationale: A modest renewal price decrease is supported for personal motor in the North West because retention and conversion weakened materially during 2025 while average quoted premium was broadly flat, suggesting the current retention concern is more closely associated with demand-side pressure than with worsening claims. Renewal retention moved from 88.0% to 74.0% and quote-to-sale conversion moved from 21.9% to 19.0% over the period, while claims loss ratio improved from 71.8% to 71.1% [retention-north_west-2025-12-01, conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, claims-north_west-2025-12-01]. External market context is also softer: the tracked fictional competitor index averaged -5.0%, and market commentary describes competitors reducing renewal prices by roughly four to six percent, with retention risk elevated for any further increase [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01, mi-retention-industry-2025-11:chunk-001]. Customer and market feedback repeatedly points to affordability pressure, price-related cancellations, and comparison shopping at renewal, which is consistent with a cautious retention response [cf-retention-affordability-2025-12:chunk-001, cf-retention-cancellation-2025-11:chunk-001, cf-retention-calls-2025-12:chunk-001, mi-retention-economic-2025-12:chunk-001]. Pricing history adds supporting context: a prior +2.0% renewal increase was associated with subsequent retention softening, while loss ratio improved [pricing-history-2024-06-01]. Within the +/-5% policy limit, a -3% to -1% range best fits the evidence as a measured retention-oriented option rather than a full match to competitor softness.
counter_evidence: Claims were modestly better, not deteriorating: loss ratio moved from 71.8% to 71.1%, which weakens the case for any urgent corrective repricing beyond a measured retention response [claims-north_west-2025-12-01].

Repair-cost intelligence showed trends broadly in line with historical norms and no clear external severity signal in either direction, so the evidence does not point to a strong cost-based reason for either a larger decrease or a larger increase [mi-retention-repair-2025-11:chunk-001].

The tracked fictional competitor movement averaged -5.0%, which is softer than the recommended range; a smaller decrease may only partially address competitive pressure [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01].

Quote-to-sale conversion and retention weakened while premium was broadly flat at portfolio level, so factors beyond own-price alone may also be present and should not be overstated [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, retention-north_west-2025-12-01].
